attack: Strongest opposing claim: the USD-down/CAD-up camp (perma-bull, value-guy) plus the AUD/NZD mean-reversion camp (cross-merchant, mean-reverter, vol-convexity) argue that 99th-percentile US yields, 87th-percentile USDCAD, 99th-percentile AUD crosses and 8th-percentile NZDUSD are late-cycle stretches that should reverse, with AU housing and CA labor as the reversal evidence.

The hole is that they treat statistical extremes as the thesis. This packet’s live changes still run the other way: US 2Y +9bp 1d and +57bp 1m after a greater-than-90% priced hike; USDCAD +1.10% 5d / +1.74% 1m; AUDNZD +4.27% 1m; NZDUSD still falling. A 4th-percentile CA-US 2Y that is still widening is not a compression trade. A 5y AUDCAD high whose 1m impulse is CAD weakness is not a CAD-up signal.

AU housing (stamp duty -24% y/y, transactions -18%, values more than 7% off peak) is a concrete local reversal for the RBA. It does not cool US gauges, unprint SOFR 3.85, or put the SR3 strip onto a cut path. Using it to fade USD or to bounce NZD skips the country that actually hiked.

value-guy’s long SOFR-CORRA needs the US-expensive leg to stop rising. The post-hike 2Y still rose. If their US-rates-down leg is how the spread compresses, that is a US fade this remit rejects. If compression is supposed to come from CORRA catching up, that is a CA hike that has not printed against labor 38 and core-near-2%. Either leg is a hope, not a trend.
